Rank spectral features by their temporal contrast across field borders

Source: R/train.R
fb_rank_contrast.Rd

For pixel pairs centred on reference field boundaries (across pairs: the two ends lie in different fields) and inside fields (within pairs), every candidate feature is summarised by the temporal maximum and mean, over dates clear at both ends, of log(|f(p) - f(q)| + 1e-4). Features are ranked by the area under the ROC curve (AUC) with which the temporal maximum separates across from within pairs, averaged over strata. This extends the class-separability screening of spectral indices (as in the svid package) from classes to field borders.

Usage

fb_rank_contrast(
  stacks,
  references,
  features = NULL,
  strata = NULL,
  n_pairs = 4000L,
  seed = 1L
)

Arguments

stacks

An fb_stack or a list of them (training tiles). For many tiles, list elements may be functions without arguments that return the stack; each tile is then loaded only while it is processed.

references

A reference raster from fb_reference() or a list of them, one per stack (or functions returning them).

features

Candidate features from fb_feature_set(); by default the bands and all normalised differences of the first stack's bands.

strata

Optional stratum label per stack; the AUC is averaged over strata.

n_pairs

Maximum number of across and of within pairs per stack.

seed

Random seed for pair sampling.

Value

An object of class fb_contrast with ranking (data frame of features with their AUC, by stratum and averaged) and the pair summaries used by fb_train().

Examples

s <- fb_example_stack("california")
f <- fb_example_files("california")
ref <- fb_reference(sf::st_read(f$fields, quiet = TRUE), s)
rk <- fb_rank_contrast(s, ref, n_pairs = 1000)
head(rk$ranking)
#>       feature type       auc   auc_all
#> 1 ND(B05,B08)   nd 0.9876176 0.9876176
#> 2 ND(B06,B08)   nd 0.9837059 0.9837059
#> 3 ND(B07,B08)   nd 0.9813235 0.9813235
#> 4 ND(B04,B08)   nd 0.9770294 0.9770294
#> 5         B08 band 0.9765735 0.9765735
#> 6 ND(B03,B08)   nd 0.9761471 0.9761471
fb_plot_ranking(rk, n = 15)
